chain.label: Dark night takeoff, no moon, about an hour before sunrise
chain.trigger: Night visual meteorological conditions (VMC) prevailed at the time of the accident.

chain.label: Unlit runway 26 and construction-altered taxiway A geometry placing the two hold short lines 560 ft apart
chain.trigger: Although the runway was equipped with runway edge lights when the width was 150 feet, these lights had been disconnected since 2001 when the runway was designated for daytime VFR use only. ... The hold short line for runway 26 was about 560 feet from the hold short line for runway 22.

chain.label: FAA did not require runway crossings to be authorized by specific ATC clearance, nor require runway confirmation or controller monitoring
chain.trigger: Contributing to the accident were ... the Federal Aviation Administration's (FAA) failure to require that all runway crossings be authorized only by specific air traffic control (ATC) clearances.

chain.label: Captain set a casual cockpit tone and gave an abbreviated taxi briefing on the crew's first flight together
chain.trigger: the captain stated 'Comair standard' instead of all of the information in that portion of the taxi briefing, including that runway 26 was to be crossed while navigating to runway 22 ... the captain told the first officer several times, 'at your leisure'

chain.label: Both pilots held nonpertinent conversation during taxi, violating the sterile cockpit rule
chain.trigger: From about 0603:16 to about 0603:56, the flight crew engaged in conversation that was not pertinent to the operation of the flight.

caused_by.evidence: The captain had the responsibility to assert both his leadership role and command authority to stop the discussion. Rather, the captain allowed the conversation to continue and participated in it.

chain.label: Crew lost positional awareness and failed to use available surface cues, stopping at the runway 26 hold short line believing it was runway 22
chain.trigger: about 0604:33, the airplane stopped on taxiway A at the hold short line for runway 26 ... At this position, the flight crew would have been able to see the runway 26 holding position sign, the '26' painted runway number

caused_by.evidence: The flight crewmembers' nonpertinent conversation during the taxi, which was not in compliance with Federal regulations and company policy, likely contributed to their loss of positional awareness.

the angle from the runway 26 hold short line on taxiway A to runway 26 was the same as the angle from the runway 22 hold short line on former taxiway A ... the taxiway A centerline split into three lines after the runway 26 hold short line
this task is more difficult during night conditions, when surrounding features in the environment and horizon as well as other cues are not easily detectable

chain.label: Crew taxied onto runway 26 and began the takeoff roll without cross-checking the heading indicator or verifying the runway
chain.trigger: the flight crewmembers failed to recognize that they were initiating a takeoff on the wrong runway because they did not cross-check and confirm the airplane's position on the runway before takeoff and they were likely influenced by confirmation bias

caused_by.evidence: The captain and the first officer believed that the airplane was on runway 22 when they taxied onto runway 26 and initiated the takeoff roll.
the Board determined that Comair and other Part 121 operators did not have procedures for positively verifying that an airplane was aligned on the correct departure runway

chain.label: Lone tower controller fatigued after about 2 hours of sleep in the preceding 24 hours on a midnight shift
chain.trigger: the controller had slept about 2 hours in the 24 hours that preceded the accident ... The controller was most likely fatigued at the time of the accident

chain.label: Controller did not monitor the taxi or takeoff, turning to an administrative traffic count and missing both windows to catch the error
chain.trigger: The controller did not detect the flight crew's attempt to take off on the wrong runway because, instead of monitoring the airplane's departure, he performed a lower-priority administrative task

caused_by.evidence: Fatigue tends to increase preoccupation with single tasks or elements, reduce scanning, increase vigilance errors, impair decision-making

The Federal Aviation Administration's operational policies and procedures at the time of the accident were deficient because they did not promote optimal controller monitoring of aircraft surface operations.

chain.label: Crew recognized the problem only past the abort point; early V1/rotate call and abrupt full-aft rotation at 131 knots
chain.trigger: the captain called, 'V one, rotate,' and stated, 'whoa' ... the control columns reached their full aft position about 0606:32 and that the airplane rotated at a rate of about 10º per second

caused_by.evidence: The flight crew recognized that something was wrong with the takeoff beyond the point from which the airplane could be stopped on the remaining available runway.

chain.label: Airplane ran off the departure end of the 3,501-foot runway 26
chain.trigger: The airplane ran off the end of the runway and impacted the airport perimeter fence, trees, and terrain.

caused_by.evidence: Bombardier calculated that a CRJ-100 would need 3,593 feet to reach a V1 speed of 135 knots and 3,744 feet to start rotation.
FDR airspeed and altitude data showed that the airplane became temporarily airborne after impacting the berm but climbed less than 20 feet off the ground.

he could have addressed this situation by alerting the flight crewmembers that the airplane was on the wrong runway or, later, by instructing them to reject the takeoff. The controller did not take any such actions.

chain.label: Impact with earthen berm, perimeter fence, and trees; airplane destroyed by impact and postcrash fire
chain.trigger: The airplane impacted an earthen berm located about 265 feet from the end of runway 26 ... the airplane impacted a tree located about 900 feet from the end of runway 26. The airplane was destroyed by impact forces and postcrash fire.

caused_by.evidence: tire marks from the left and right main landing gear and the nose landing gear were found in the grass immediately off the end of the runway

chain.label: 49 occupants killed by blunt force injuries and postcrash fire; first officer seriously injured
chain.trigger: The captain, flight attendant, and 47 passengers were killed, and the first officer received serious injuries.

caused_by.evidence: The simultaneous impacts with two large diameter trees caused numerous blunt force fatal injuries to passengers ... these occupants survived the impact but succumbed to the effects of the postcrash fire and smoke.
